title: Priority buckets + credit-slicing with regional spillover for tiered traffic
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a tier-aware routing layer that enforces per-tenant/plan credit buckets (free/paid/enterprise), slices burst credits, and enables controlled regional spillover and model-variant fallbacks when capacity or credits are constrained.
background: We currently route requests by simple tier mapping with a blunt quota enforcement that returns 429s when exceeded. Customers with mixed plans (free -> paid) experience poor UX during regional outages and burst usage. Product requests a softer degradation path that preserves enterprise SLAs while offering best-effort processing for paid and free users with graceful fallbacks to cheaper model variants or alternate regions.
proposal: Introduce three coordinated mechanisms: (1) priority buckets per tenant plan (enterprise > paid > free) with token-credit accounting and burst reservoirs; (2) credit-slicing engine that lets paid tiers borrow soft credits from short-lived burst pool based on historical cadence and fairness; (3) regional spillover policy and a model-variant degradation ladder (full-pro, quantized-pro, small-proxy) that routing can select automatically when local capacity or credits are low.
design_decisions:
- Use per-tenant credit ledger stored in Redis with atomic Lua ops for debit/peek to avoid race conditions.
- Implement soft-decrement semantics: when soft credits exhausted, route to lower-cost variant; when hard credits exhausted, return 429 for free tier but enqueue low-priority paid requests to a deferred queue instead of immediate failure.
- Regional spillover is enabled only for paid+enterprise tiers and gated by geographic latency thresholds (max added tail 80th <= 150ms).
- Model-variant compatibility matrix declared in catalog metadata; runtime performs compatibility check before automatic fallback.
- Metrics emitted include credit_balance, credit_burn_rate, fallback_rate_by_tier, regional_spill_count, avg_added_latency_by_spill.
tradeoffs:
- Pros: better customer experience, fewer hard failures, controllable cost.
- Cons: additional operational complexity and state (credit ledger), potential for unexpected cross-region egress cost, subtle fairness issues if burst pools are abused.
- Mitigations: rate-limited borrow, per-tenant daily borrow budget, autoscaling cost alerting and budget caps for spillover.
acceptance_criteria:
- Credit ledger updates are atomic and pass concurrency fuzz tests.
- For synthetic load tests, free tier sees graceful 429 behavior after soft fallback attempts.
- Paid tier can borrow from burst pool under controlled conditions; borrow rate adheres to configured per-tenant caps.
- Regional spillover triggers under simulated region-constrained tests and falls back to alternate region with <200ms added tail latency to enterprise traffic.
- Telemetry surfaces fallback reasons and per-tier SLA adherence.
- End-to-end integration test in staging with realistic workload passes without data loss.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag behind routing.priority_buckets and routing.spillover, off by default.
2) Canary: enable for 2 internal tenants with low traffic and telemetry only.
3) Beta: enable for a subset of paid customers with monitoring and on-call runbook.
4) Gradual: expand to all paid then enterprise tenants after 2 weeks stability.
5) GA: enable for free tier with conservative defaults.
Links: Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Smart+Routing+Priority+Buckets, rollout checklist PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prod-config/pull/842
monitoring:
Primary metrics: credit_balance.{tenant}, credit_burn_rate.{tenant}, fallback_rate.{tier}, regional_spill_count.{region}, request_latency_added_by_spill.{percentile}.
SLOs: enterprise 99.9% requests served by primary model without >=200ms extra latency; paid target 99% within fallback ladder; free best-effort.
Alerts: fallback_rate spike > 5% for enterprise; borrow_rate breach > configured cap; unexpected cross-region egress > $500/day.
Dashboards: /dashboards/routing/priority-buckets
test_plan:
- Unit tests for credit ledger operations and Lua scripts.
- Integration tests: multi-tenant charge and refund flows, borrow/repay cycles.
- Chaos test: fail a region (simulate AZ/region outage) and verify spillover + fallback behavior.
- Load test: 10k TPS synthetic mix (70% free, 25% paid, 5% enterprise) to validate burst pool behavior and fairness.
- Security test: KMS-encrypted ledger keys and access control checks.
implementation_notes:
- Runtime: add middleware layer in router service to consult Credit API before dispatch.
- Credit API: new service with Redis primary store and Postgres durable snapshots for audit.
- Configs: tier policies in /configs/tier-policies.yaml; allow per-tenant overrides via admin console.
- Compatibility: update model catalog to include fallback ladder entries, signal via model_meta.fallbacks.
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/310, https://github.com/redwood-inference/credit-api/pull/29
